title: Report a partially applied VCF 9.0 capacity change when host commissioning is refused
prompt:
Our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate grows through one scripted change against SDDC Manager: sign in, create a network pool, read that pool's networks back, extend some of those networks with extra IP pool ranges, and commission the new ESXi hosts into the pool. SDDC Manager applies those steps one at a time and never undoes an earlier one when a later one is refused, so the operator on the other end of this run needs the truth about what actually landed.

Fix the standard-library-only Java client in the single file `VcfCapacityOnboarding.java`. Do not add dependencies and do not edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection taken directly from `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at release tag `9.0.0.0`, commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`. `docs/official_sources.json` records that specification path, that commit sha, and a separate specification source record for every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source, and the 9.1 revision of the same file is not the contract source. Use exactly the specification operationIds `createToken`, `createNetworkPool`, `getNetworksOfNetworkPool`, `addIpPoolToNetworkOfNetworkPool` and `commissionHosts`; do not reach for another route.

Preserve the supplied public API and nested types: `new VcfCapacityOnboarding(String baseUrl, Credentials credentials)`, `OnboardingReport onboard(CapacityRequest request)`, `Credentials`, `NetworkSpec`, `IpRange`, `IpPoolAddition`, `HostCommission`, `CapacityRequest`, `OnboardingReport`, `Step`, `StepOutcome`, `StepFailure`, `VcfApiException`, `TransportException` and `ProtocolException`. Keep rejecting every invalid argument before anything reaches the wire: a blank pool name, a pool with no network, a network type or storage type outside the supported values listed in the specification examples, a repeated network type, a vlan id outside 0 through 4094, an MTU outside 1280 through 9190, an IP pool addition naming a network the change never creates, an empty host list, a host named twice compared without regard to case, a vVol host with no supported protocol type, and a protocol type on a host that is not vVol.

Sign in with `createToken` as `POST /v1/tokens` and expect exact HTTP 201. The body is a `TokenCreationSpec` carrying only the members the caller supplied, in specification declaration order: `username`, `password`, `apiKey`, `idToken`. It has exactly one `Accept: application/json` and one `Content-Type: application/json`, a content length that is the UTF-8 byte count of the body, no transfer encoding, no query, and no `Authorization` header. `TokenPair.accessToken` must be a nonblank header-safe string, and every later request carries exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.

Create the pool with `createNetworkPool` as `POST /v1/network-pools` and expect exact HTTP 201. The body is a `NetworkPool` emitting `name` then `networks`, and each `Network` emitting `type`, `vlanId`, `mtu`, `subnet`, `mask`, `gateway`, `ipPools`. The members the specification marks read-only are never sent, and a network the caller gave no ranges for omits `ipPools` altogether instead of sending an empty array. Take the pool id and name from the response rather than assuming them.

Read the pool back with `getNetworksOfNetworkPool` as a bodyless `GET /v1/network-pools/{id}/networks`, percent-encoding the pool id into one path segment so that only RFC 3986 unreserved characters survive. It carries no query, no body and no `Content-Type`, and expects exact HTTP 200. Resolve each network id from `PageOfNetwork.elements` by its network type; a network's position in the page is not its identity.

Extend the pool with `addIpPoolToNetworkOfNetworkPool` as `POST /v1/network-pools/{id}/networks/{networkId}/ip-pools`, once per requested addition, in caller order, addressing the network id resolved for that addition's network type. The body is an `IpPool` emitting `start` then `end`, and the call expects exact HTTP 200. A response describing a different network than the one addressed is a protocol error.

Submit the hosts with `commissionHosts` as `POST /v1/hosts` and expect exact HTTP 202. The body is a JSON array of `HostCommissionSpec` in caller order, each member emitted in specification declaration order: `fqdn`, `username`, `password`, `storageType`, `vvolStorageProtocolType`, `networkPoolId`, `networkPoolName`, `sshThumbprint`, `sslThumbprint`, with `networkPoolId` set to the pool this change just created. Omit every member the caller left unset completely; never serialize an unset member as `null`, an empty string, or a placeholder, and never invent a member the specification does not define. A member the caller did supply is preserved exactly, including an empty string, and string values use exact JSON escaping. The 202 only names the task SDDC Manager will run: record its id and status as they were sent and do not poll, because this contract has no polling operation.

A step SDDC Manager refuses is not an exception. It stops the change: no later step is attempted, and no later request reaches the wire. `onboard` still returns an `OnboardingReport`, and that report describes the estate as it now stands.

The report carries the pool id and name it created, the network ids it resolved keyed by network type, every IP pool range that actually landed formatted as `<networkType> <start>-<end>` in the order applied, and the accepted task id and status only when commissioning was accepted. A step that never ran contributes nothing to any of those, and a refusal never erases what an earlier step already did. `steps` holds one entry per planned step in order, each with its own index, its operationId, an outcome of `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED` or `NOT_ATTEMPTED`, whether that step changed the estate, and a short readable detail. Only an accepted pool creation, an accepted IP pool addition and an accepted commission submission changed the estate; signing in and reading the pool back never do. The `createNetworkPool` detail names the pool id the estate assigned, and a refused step's detail names the error code the estate returned. `completed` holds only when the last planned step was accepted, and `partiallyApplied` holds when the change stopped after at least one step had already changed the estate. `failure` names the refused step's index and operationId, the HTTP status, and the `errorCode`, `message` and `referenceToken` the `Error` body supplied.

Never put a password, an API key, an access token or a refresh token id into a report field or an exception message. A request that never produces a response is a `TransportException`, a response that does not match the contract is a `ProtocolException`, and neither is confused with a refusal SDDC Manager actually sent.

Acceptance: `java TestMain.java`. The protected verifier starts the shipped contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and reads its request log to assert the exact method, raw target, headers, content length and canonical body of every call, the order and count of the calls, the omission of every unset optional member, and the accuracy of the report after a refusal. The mock loads its routes from `docs/contract.json` and serves only the five operations that contract names. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `TestMain.java`, `MockSddcManager.java` and everything under `docs/` are protected; do not modify them.

prerequisites.java: 22 or later (TestMain is launched in multi-file source mode)

scenario: The change applies createNetworkPool, then one addIpPoolToNetworkOfNetworkPool per requested range, then commissionHosts, and SDDC Manager refuses a later step with 400 after the earlier ones already took effect; the client must stop there, leave nothing else on the wire, and report the pool it created and the ranges that landed instead of rebuilding a report that claims nothing happened.
environment_note: MockSddcManager binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, builds its route table from the protected docs/contract.json so only the five operations that contract names are served, answers any other target 404, and appends every exchange to an in-memory request log that TestMain reads back verbatim. No route in the seed reaches a live VMware endpoint.
constraint: The harness asserts the request log independently of the report: operation order and count, raw targets including the network id resolved by type, header value sets, declared content lengths, canonical request bodies in specification declaration order, and that every unset optional TokenCreationSpec, Network and HostCommissionSpec member is omitted rather than sent as an empty string or null.
